findings.title: The mods folder has no checkout fallback
quotes: else the checkout's `tools/claude-mods`
return Path(__file__).parent / "mods"
findings.fix: restore the CT-8 branches in `src/nio/hooks.py:mods_dir`: the package folder if it exists, else `Path(__file__).parents[2] / "tools/claude-mods"`, else raise `ValueError`.

sources.situation: CT-8 says `mods_dir()` returns the package's `mods` folder when it exists, otherwise the checkout's `tools/claude-mods`, and raises `ValueError("no NIO mods in this nio install")` when neither exists. The code returns only `Path(__file__).parent / "mods"`. In a NIO checkout installed in editable mode (`uv sync`), the wheel's force-include is not copied, so `src/nio/mods` does not exist. `nio mods install` then passes that missing path to `claude plugin install --marketplace`, and each mod's outcome line reads `failed`. The checkout is the case CT-8 keeps working.

nio runs from an editable install or a checkout. `src/nio/mods` is absent, so `mods_dir()` points at a missing folder and `claude plugin install ... --marketplace <missing>` fails for both mods. CT-8 says to return `tools/claude-mods` when `nio/mods` doesn't exist, and to raise `ValueError` when neither exists.

findings.reason: src/nio/hooks.py:36-38 `mods_dir` returns only `Path(__file__).parent / "mods"`; CT-8 (contracts.md:90-91) requires the `tools/claude-mods` fallback and a `ValueError`, and neither exists in the code.

findings.fix: resolve the repo root first (for example with `records.repo_root()`, as the other commands do) and pass that to `mods_install`.

sources.situation: CT-10 says `plugin list` and `plugin install ... --scope local` run "in `root`", and the contract accepts "the repo root". The CLI branch passes `Path.cwd()`, the directory the human ran it from. Run from `src/`, the local-scope install is recorded for that folder, not the clone. A second run from the root then reads "not installed" and installs again.

quotes: except (ValueError, OSError) as e:
findings.fix: use `except Exception` for the juries and timeline sections, as for the others.

sources.situation: a damaged or odd-shaped ledger raises KeyError or TypeError in `juries`. It isn't caught, so the whole `flow show` call dies with `error:` on stderr and no JSON. findings.title: Pane reads jury findings from a key the CLI never sets
quotes: ...(g.findings ?? []).map((f: any) =>
rounds.append({"round": n, "lenses": lenses, "findings": [
findings.fix: render `r.findings` inside the rounds map, and add a pane test whose fixture is the real `flow show` output rather than a hand-written shape.

sources.situation: `flow.juries` returns `{"gate", "outcome", "rounds": [{"round", "lenses", "findings"}]}`, with findings inside each round. The pane's `jury` reads `g.findings` at the gate level. That key is undefined, so `?? []` hides it and every jury shows only its rounds and verdicts. Findings, severities, validations and the fix-task links (FR-5) never appear, and no error is shown. A blocked jury looks the same as an approved one apart from the word "block".

findings.reason: flow.py:987 puts `findings` inside each round and the returned gate dict (flow.py:990) has no gate-level `findings`. register.tsx:235 reads `g.findings ?? []`, so it is always empty.

findings.title: `claude plugin` calls have no timeout, so the install can hang with no output
quotes: r = subprocess.run([claude, *args], cwd=root, capture_output=True, text=True)
findings.fix: pass `timeout=` and `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL`, and map `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` to a `failed: timed out` line.

sources.situation: `claude plugin list` or `claude plugin install` blocks on a prompt, a network fetch or a lock held by another running claude. `subprocess.run` waits forever, and so do `nio mods install` and the install skill step that calls it. The docstring says "never raises, one mod failing never stops the other". A hang means the second mod never gets a line and no result is reported. Stdin is also left inherited, so an interactive prompt can swallow the terminal.

findings.reason: hooks.py:45 calls `subprocess.run` with no `timeout` and no `stdin`. CT-10 says "Never raises", and nothing bounds the wait.

findings.title: `flow show`, a read command, writes into the worktree
quotes: (path.parent / ".gitignore").write_text("*\n")
findings.fix: open the index read-only, or return `[]` when `.nio/cache/index.db` is absent. Keep the `.gitignore` write out of `connect` calls that only read.

sources.situation: `memory()` calls `index.connect(root)`, which does `mkdir`, writes `.nio/cache/.gitignore` and creates `index.db`. A click on a row in a worktree that has never been indexed therefore creates files in that worktree. This goes against FR-10's "reading the status writes nothing in the worktree". `usage.so_far` is labelled "Writes nothing", and the pane's `ENV` sets `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE` for the same reason. The write is not atomic either: two clicks at once can race on the `.gitignore` existence check. The code swallows every error from `memory` into `{"error"}`, so an unwritable or read-only worktree shows a memory error rather than the real cause.
